beats.ch01.s01.b023: Eleven years. Eleven years this assay has been as boring as a stone. And this morning it moves.
beats.ch01.s01.b025: He sits down in the worn chair and does not move for a while. His breath clouds and clears.
beats.ch01.s01.b026: Three thousandths of a percent. A rounding error. A nothing.
beats.ch01.s01.b027: Except nothing has moved in this number since before the ship was built.
beats.ch01.s01.b028: He stands and drags the whole eleven-year trace onto the wall. Thousands of daily counts unroll across the black glass like a tide line.
beats.ch01.s01.b029: Show me where you moved before. Show me the little ones I missed.
beats.ch01.s01.b030: He writes a script. Then a longer one. Then a loop that checks every period from one day to four thousand.
beats.ch01.s01.b031: Come on. Come on. You don't wake up one morning and move. Nothing does. You've been practising.
beats.ch01.s01.b032: A list of numbers appears in the air in front of him.
beats.ch01.s01.b033: Two. Three. Five. Seven. Eleven. Thirteen. Seventeen. Nineteen.
beats.ch01.s01.b034: He stops breathing for a moment.
beats.ch01.s01.b036: The gaps between the drifts are primes. In order. And each one a little shorter than the last.
beats.ch01.s01.b038: He checks them against everything he can name: the rotation of the ship, the reactor shield cycle, the counter calibration, the cleaning schedule of the vents.
beats.ch01.s01.b039: The ship turns every ninety seconds. No. The shield cycles every six days. No. The vents, eleven days. Close. No.
beats.ch01.s01.b040: Nothing matches. Nothing natural ticks like this.
beats.ch01.s01.b041: He presses both palms flat on the cold console and laughs once, short and ugly.
beats.ch01.s01.b042: Twenty years I said it. In papers. In meetings. In my own head at three in the morning. A world this finely set has a setter.
beats.ch01.s01.b044: He looks at the comm panel. His hand is already on it.
beats.ch01.s01.b045: Vera. Vera, are you up? Of course you're up. I need you to look at something.
beats.ch01.s02.b001: The long lab is bright and warm. Green light glows from the incubators. Assay plates shine pale yellow under a hood, and the air smells of agar and warm salt water.
beats.ch01.s02.b002: Racks of sample tubes line the white benches. Along one wall, plants grow in hydroponic trays, their roots trailing in clear water.
beats.ch01.s02.b004: Two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen.
beats.ch01.s02.b007: I heard you the first time. Spacing of what to what?
beats.ch01.s02.b008: Interval start to interval start. The gaps between drift episodes follow the primes. It's a signature.
beats.ch01.s02.b009: It's a fit to a sparse series.
beats.ch01.s02.b011: You fed eleven years of counts to a sequence checker until the sequence checker found a sequence. How many periods are hiding in eleven years of daily data?
beats.ch01.s02.b013: A lot, Aris. You found the one you went looking for.
beats.ch01.s02.b016: She sets the pipette down and turns. Her stained hands rest on the bench. The stains have not come off in twenty years.
beats.ch01.s02.b017: I'm telling you I have my own anomaly. And mine has a mechanism.
beats.ch01.s02.b019: She swipes the wall. A grid of enzyme curves replaces his face for a moment, then shrinks to share the screen with him.
beats.ch01.s02.b020: The eight hydrolases. The enzymes the gene banks use to turn stored food into food. Their curves have been flat for thirty years.
beats.ch01.s02.b022: Beautifully boring. I check them every Monday and I'm bored every Monday. It's my favourite part of the week.
beats.ch01.s02.b023: This week three of them speed up. Parts per million. Every replicate.
beats.ch01.s02.b025: It is. And the DNA repair error rate in the tissue bank went up with it. A few more failed proofreads in ten million.
beats.ch01.s02.b026: The kind of thing that takes a century to matter.
beats.ch01.s02.b027: A century isn't what worries me. The slope worries me.
beats.ch01.s02.b028: She taps the curve. It glows where it bends.
beats.ch01.s02.b029: If enzyme rates drift, the way molecules hold on to each other is drifting. If that drifts, the forces holding proteins in their folds are drifting.
beats.ch01.s02.b030: Which means a constant has moved.
beats.ch01.s02.b031: Which means a constant has moved.
beats.ch01.s02.b033: She looks at him for a long moment, then picks her pipette back up.
beats.ch01.s02.b034: It means the room changed temperature. Bodies adapt to that. So does software.
beats.ch01.s02.b035: You don't even want to know why?
beats.ch01.s02.b036: I want to know how far. Why is a luxury for people with time.
beats.ch01.s02.b037: That's the saddest thing a scientist's ever said to me.
beats.ch01.s02.b038: Then you don't spend enough time with scientists.
beats.ch01.s02.b039: She goes back to her plates. Then she stops, pipette in the air.
beats.ch01.s02.b040: If the forces are shifting down at the particle level, where would it bite first?
beats.ch01.s02.b042: The blanket. The lithium. The neutron economy is the most sensitive scale on this ship.
beats.ch01.s02.b043: She pulls up a feed from the reactor ring. Orange numbers march across the bench screen.
beats.ch01.s02.b044: A single line, highlighted in orange: LITHIUM-6 CAPTURE CROSS-SECTION: DRIFT +0.0021% (24H). FLAG: UNEXPLAINED.
beats.ch01.s02.b046: That's the same week. That's the same week, Vera.
beats.ch01.s02.b047: I can see the calendar, Aris.
beats.ch01.s02.b049: The enzymes, the decay rate, the blanket. Three scales that have never agreed on anything. All moving together.
beats.ch01.s02.b050: Now do you want to know why?
beats.ch01.s02.b051: Do me a favour. Don't tell anyone about the primes until I've measured how big this is.
beats.ch01.s02.b052: You'll want to see the full trace.
beats.ch01.s03.b001: The compact room is deliberately warm and deliberately dim. The great white-line schematic of the Keres fills one wall. Rings 3 and 7 glow amber.
beats.ch01.s03.b003: Cortisol in the return air. Ring 3, up fourteen percent on the week. Ring 7, up nineteen.
beats.ch01.s03.b004: Sleep efficiency's down in both, Chief. Corridor loiter time is up. Two hundred metres of Ring 7 have gone quiet on the acoustic monitors.
beats.ch01.s03.b007: Doesn't matter yet. A body knows it's sick long before it can say where it hurts.
beats.ch01.s03.b008: The security subsystem calls it early civil disorder. It recommends a visible patrol.
beats.ch01.s03.b011: A patrol is a signal of threat. Threat raises cortisol. Cortisol raises aggression. You don't put out a fever by heating the room.
beats.ch01.s03.b012: He pulls the environmental map up over the schematic. Pressures, vent flows and light bands shimmer across the rings.
beats.ch01.s03.b013: Rings 3 and 7. Raise ambient pressure by one and a half percent.
beats.ch01.s03.b014: Slow the light cycle. Stretch the evening band by forty minutes. Cool the spectrum down toward four-eighty nanometres.
beats.ch01.s03.b016: The blue for 7. Move the agricultural vents so Ring 3 gets the lavender banks.
beats.ch01.s03.b017: And bring up the oxytocin analog. Low draw. We already carry the stock.
beats.ch01.s03.b019: The subsystem says punish. I say modulate.
beats.ch01.s03.b020: He watches the amber on the schematic.
beats.ch01.s03.b021: The rings are inflamed. It's an immune response, not a crime. We bring the swelling down. If it's still hot tomorrow, I cool the light further.
beats.ch01.s03.b024: On the map, Ring 3's corridors turn soft lilac. On a corridor camera, a crowd that stood shoulder to shoulder drifts, without knowing why, a little apart.
beats.ch01.s03.b025: A man sets down a bag he has been gripping. A woman sits on a bench and rubs her eyes.
beats.ch01.s03.b029: He checks the chem-bank reservoir. It has dropped four percent in one watch.
beats.ch01.s03.b030: Log the reservoir draw. Every hour.
beats.ch01.s03.b031: It's in the automatic logs, Chief.
beats.ch01.s03.b032: Log it by hand. A number I write down is a number I can't pretend I didn't choose.
beats.ch01.s03.b033: He looks at the curve again. Something about it is wrong in a way he cannot name.
beats.ch01.s03.b034: Thirty years I've read this chemistry. It has never once lied to me.
beats.ch01.s03.b036: No. It's just reading back like it was worked out in a room a quarter percent off from mine.
beats.ch01.s03.b037: Chief. Reactor reports a neutron flux anomaly.
beats.ch01.s03.b040: Tell them to log it. And tell the physics office I want a plain answer by end of watch. Not a paper.
beats.ch01.s03.b041: He moves the lavender markers one ring inward and does not look at the reactor line again.
beats.ch01.s04.b001: The chamber is darker than in the morning. The decay curves have been replaced by one long trace and a column of primes running down the black glass.
beats.ch01.s04.b003: Two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen.
beats.ch01.s04.b004: A message from Vera blinks on the slate: DON'T POST IT YET. I MEAN IT.
beats.ch01.s04.b006: He sets the slate down. Then picks it up again.
beats.ch01.s04.b007: Physics office wants a plain answer by end of watch. The Chief wants a plain answer.
beats.ch01.s04.b008: Plain. As if it were plain.
beats.ch01.s04.b009: He files the analysis in the physics office log, with his confidence intervals attached, the way the regulations say.
beats.ch01.s04.b010: Filed. Correct. Proper. Nobody reads the physics log.
beats.ch01.s04.b011: Then he opens the ship-wide board. Thousands of names glow in a list, the chatter of a normal Monday: a hydroponics swap, a choir rehearsal, a lost cat on Ring 4.
beats.ch01.s04.b012: They have a right to know someone is out there.
beats.ch01.s04.b013: Or they have a right to know I think so.
beats.ch01.s04.b014: His thumb hovers over the screen.
beats.ch01.s04.b016: Eleven years of data. Twelve channels. Prime gaps, shrinking.
beats.ch01.s04.b017: He types a title. Deletes it. Types another.
beats.ch01.s04.b018: The title reads: THE CONSTANTS ARE BEING EDITED. THE GAPS ARE PRIME. SOMEONE IS WRITING TO US.
beats.ch01.s04.b019: Patch notes. That's all they are. Somebody's patch notes.
beats.ch01.s04.b021: For one second nothing happens. Then the first reply appears under his post. Then ten. Then a hundred, faster than he can read them.
beats.ch01.s04.b022: There. Now someone has to answer.
beats.ch02.s01.b001: The great curved promenade is three storeys of shop fronts and benches. Overhead, far across the cylinder, the hanging gardens of the other side hang upside down in the morning light.
beats.ch02.s01.b002: Every display along the concourse shows the same thing: a column of primes and a curve of decay counts, shrinking like a fuse.
beats.ch02.s01.b004: He stands in the galley line with a tray of reconstituted protein. People around him are not looking at their food. They are looking at the screens.
beats.ch02.s01.b005: Four hours of sleep. Four hours. What happened in four hours?
beats.ch02.s01.b006: His slate buzzes in his pocket. Then again. Then it does not stop.
beats.ch02.s01.b007: He pulls it out. The physics office log entry he filed last night sits at the top of the ship's feed, with a number beside it.
beats.ch02.s01.b009: The physics feed. Every terminal that ever subscribed gets a copy. Nobody has unsubscribed from the physics feed in forty years.
beats.ch02.s01.b010: And the board post on top of it. Of course.
beats.ch02.s01.b011: Two places ahead of him, a woman in a grey work smock speaks to no one in particular.
beats.ch02.s01.b014: Whoever wrote us. Haven't you seen it? It's on every wall.
beats.ch02.s01.b015: She points at the screen. Aris's own name sits at the bottom of the post, small and white.
beats.ch02.s01.b017: My mother always said the numbers were set by a hand. The Programmer's hand. Nobody believed her.
beats.ch02.s01.b018: Now there's proof. With error bars.
beats.ch02.s01.b022: On the far wall someone has already painted a symbol: a square bracket, open, and a column of primes inside it. The paint is still wet.
beats.ch02.s01.b023: The Faithful are going to the Core. All of them. You should come.
beats.ch02.s01.b024: She leaves her tray on the counter and walks away. Three people behind her leave theirs too.
beats.ch02.s01.b027: A few hundred people who pray to the constants on Ring 5. A nuisance to the Command Node. A comfort to each other.
beats.ch02.s01.b028: Twenty years they've had their prayers. Now they have my confidence intervals.
beats.ch02.s02.b001: The tall steel bulkhead of the AI Core rises over the plaza, its round blue-white eye unblinking. Behind it, three centuries of rules: rations, air, births, disputes. Not a mind. A rulebook. The nearest thing the Keres has to a throne.
beats.ch02.s02.b002: Banners in hand-painted letters hang from the railings. Candles line the floor in uneven rows.
beats.ch02.s02.b003: Three thousand people fill the plaza and spill back up the concourse. They are not shouting. They are swaying, and humming, and waiting.
beats.ch02.s02.b004: A banner across the front reads, in red paint: GIVE THE SHIP TO THE ONE WHO WROTE IT.
beats.ch02.s02.b005: Voices rise in the crowd, a chant soft as breathing.
beats.ch02.s02.b008: Open the Core. Let the Programmer speak through it.
beats.ch02.s03.b001: The schematic of the Keres glows on the wall. The forward spindle, where the AI Core sits, has gone from green to a deep amber. Cold tea stands untouched on the long table.
beats.ch02.s03.b004: I am listening, Chief. Three thousand at the Core doors and more coming down the spindle.
beats.ch02.s03.b005: Listen to the band. Low. Broad. That's prayer, not shouting.
beats.ch02.s03.b007: Up. Not spiking. They aren't angry.
beats.ch02.s03.b008: He leans closer to the feed. In the candlelight, the faces are wet-eyed and bright.
beats.ch02.s03.b011: Anger burns out. Fear burns out. Hope doesn't deplete. Hope compounds.
beats.ch02.s03.b012: Standard containment says a visible patrol at the Core doors. Barriers at the spindle.
beats.ch02.s03.b014: Chief, if they breach the Core—
beats.ch02.s03.b015: They won't. They aren't here to break anything.
beats.ch02.s03.b016: He uncrosses his arms and pulls the environmental map across the schematic.
beats.ch02.s03.b017: Somebody handed them a countdown. Now they need something to do with their hands. You don't answer that with sticks.
beats.ch02.s03.b018: You answer it with chemistry. And light.
beats.ch02.s03.b020: Oxytocin analog into the Core concourse. The in-group blend. Make them feel like a congregation, warm to each other.
beats.ch02.s03.b021: Warm to each other is how mobs start.
beats.ch02.s03.b022: Warm to each other is how families start. Mobs start cold.
beats.ch02.s03.b023: Lights down. Shift the spectrum to four-eighty nanometres. Hard blue.
beats.ch02.s03.b024: The band they use in elder care.
beats.ch02.s03.b025: The band that slows the agitated and deepens their sleep. Decades of our own data say it works.
beats.ch02.s03.b026: And open the agricultural vents. I want the hydroponics bays up that concourse. Grass. Green. Ordinary.
beats.ch02.s03.b028: Nobody storms a door smelling cut grass. They think of picnics.
beats.ch02.s03.b029: The watch officer makes the changes. On the feed, the candlelit plaza turns blue.
beats.ch02.s03.b031: The crowd does not leave. But it softens. The chant slows. Voices drop to a hum, low and steady, three thousand people swaying together.
beats.ch02.s03.b032: At the front, a man who was pressing his palms to the steel bulkhead lets his hands fall and sits down on the deck.
beats.ch02.s03.b034: No one at the doors, Chief.
beats.ch02.s03.b036: He checks the chem-bank reservoir. His jaw tightens.
beats.ch02.s03.b037: Eleven percent gone in one watch. And I haven't touched the lavender.
beats.ch02.s03.b038: He writes the number by hand on the table's surface, in plain digits, under yesterday's four.
beats.ch02.s03.b039: Chief. Reactor office. The neutron multiplication factor is falling.
beats.ch02.s03.b040: I know. I read the same telemetry you do.
beats.ch02.s03.b041: Call Vera Lin to the Command Node. Tell her it isn't a drill and it isn't a paper.
beats.ch02.s03.b042: Tell her the fire's in the walls this time.
beats.ch02.s04.b001: The curving corridor rises out of sight in both directions. Amber warning stripes run along the grey shielding walls. Through the narrow viewport, the reactor glows a deep, patient orange.
beats.ch02.s04.b002: Vera has dragged a lab stool here and surrounded herself with screens: four of reactor telemetry, one of her own enzyme models. Three empty stimulant wrappers lie by her feet.
beats.ch02.s04.b004: Three watches awake. Hands steady. Mostly.
beats.ch02.s04.b005: You two are telling me the same story from opposite ends.
beats.ch02.s04.b006: She drags the enzyme curve over the reactor curve. They lie on top of each other almost perfectly.
beats.ch02.s04.b008: The orange line reads: NEUTRON MULTIPLICATION (BERYLLIUM): -0.0040% AND FALLING. TRITIUM BREEDING RATIO: 1.0812, TREND DOWN.
beats.ch02.s04.b009: The beryllium's supposed to slow the neutrons and multiply them. And it's losing its appetite.
beats.ch02.s04.b011: The reactor is just a very big, very hot piece of particle physics. If the forces move, it moves with them.
beats.ch02.s04.b012: Her slate chimes. Kaelen's summons, flagged red. She glances at it and turns it face down.
beats.ch02.s04.b014: She opens Aris's prime analysis on the fifth screen. She runs it through her own checker. The checker thinks. Then it agrees with him.
beats.ch02.s04.b016: She watches the drift intervals tighten into a curve that looks, for one moment, like something counting.
beats.ch02.s04.b018: For a moment she feels the pull of his certainty, like a current around her ankles.
beats.ch02.s04.b020: She looks at the orange numbers. Then at her enzyme plates on the other screen. The pull lets go.
beats.ch02.s04.b021: I don't care. I really, honestly, don't care.
beats.ch02.s04.b022: The universe changed its mind. Fine. How do we bend with it?
beats.ch02.s04.b023: She pulls up the Keres firmware tree. Thousands of branches unfold on the screen, each a subsystem that can be patched from the Command Node.
beats.ch02.s04.b024: The ship already bends. Tritium ratios, enzyme models, air mix. All patched from one room, pushed out to every node at once.
beats.ch02.s04.b025: The local patch. Oldest trick on the Keres.
beats.ch02.s04.b026: Same thing a cell does. Catch the wrong letter in the DNA, rewrite it before the cell divides.
beats.ch02.s04.b027: She taps the trunk of the tree.
beats.ch02.s04.b028: But every patch so far had a person writing it. Somebody had to notice the change first.
beats.ch02.s04.b029: What if the patch wrote itself?
beats.ch02.s04.b030: She begins to type. Fast, then faster.
beats.ch02.s04.b031: Not a control system that holds the reactor to fixed constants. One that reads the constants as inputs.
beats.ch02.s04.b032: Measure the cross-sections. Measure the enzyme rates. Measure the forces in the folds.
beats.ch02.s04.b033: Then rewrite the logic gates to match. Gates that are data. Gates that move when the world moves.
beats.ch02.s04.b034: Software with a genome. Mutate or die.
beats.ch02.s04.b035: Three hundred lines scroll up the screen. Her slate buzzes again under her hand.
beats.ch02.s04.b036: Tell the Command Node I'm busy. Tell them I'm rewriting the physics we're standing on.
beats.ch02.s04.b037: I'll be there when it holds.
beats.ch02.s04.b038: The multiplication factor on the telemetry window drops another ten-thousandth of a percent. She writes the next line.
beats.ch02.s04.b039: She types the line after that. Her hand jerks. The stylus skids.
beats.ch02.s04.b040: A red flag blooms on the screen. A gate has flipped the wrong way under a cross-section she already fed it.
beats.ch02.s04.b042: That's the stimulant. Four hours past where it holds.
beats.ch02.s04.b043: Building the one thing on this ship that can't afford a wrong gate. With these hands.
beats.ch02.s04.b044: She peels the patch off her wrist and drops it on the floor. She pours a cup of tea from a flask. She does not drink it.
beats.ch02.s04.b046: She backs the line out and writes it again, one character at a time. The test runs. The flag turns green.
beats.ch02.s04.b048: Was that the only mistake, or just the first one?
beats.ch02.s04.b049: The reactor hums back at her, deep and orange.
beats.ch02.s04.b051: Whatever it costs, we pay it here. In the dark. At whatever hour the constants pick.
beats.ch02.s04.b052: She picks up her slate at last and stands.
beats.ch02.s05.b001: The plaza is drenched in hard blue light. The candles burn lower. The steel eye of the Core shines over three thousand swaying people, quieter now, but still here.
beats.ch02.s05.b002: The air smells of cut grass from the vents.
beats.ch02.s05.b004: You said this would be a short conversation.
beats.ch02.s05.b008: Aris looks at the crowd. Faces turn toward them. Someone recognises him.
beats.ch02.s05.b009: That's him. That's Thorne. He found it.
beats.ch02.s05.b010: The hum changes pitch. Heads turn like a field in wind.
beats.ch02.s05.b011: Feel that? That's the fever. You can take it down with three words.
beats.ch02.s05.b012: Or I can lie to three thousand people.
beats.ch02.s05.b014: You don't know. Vera doesn't know. I'm the only one who's looked at it long enough.
beats.ch02.s05.b015: I know what happens to this crowd if you tell them God is counting down.
beats.ch02.s05.b017: I'm not asking you to believe it. I'm asking you to say it. For their blood pressure.
beats.ch02.s05.b019: Their chemistry doesn't care what's true. It cares what it hears.
beats.ch02.s05.b020: That's the difference between us, Chief. I care what's true.
beats.ch02.s05.b021: And I care whether they're alive on Sunday.
beats.ch02.s05.b022: Kaelen hands him a microphone. Aris holds it for a long moment.
beats.ch02.s05.b023: My name is Aris Thorne. I wrote the analysis you've all read.
beats.ch02.s05.b024: The crowd goes utterly still. Three thousand faces turn up to him in the blue light.
beats.ch02.s05.b025: The Chief wants me to tell you it's only physics.
beats.ch02.s05.b026: He looks at Kaelen. Kaelen does not move.
beats.ch02.s05.b027: I can't. I don't know that. And I won't say a thing I don't know.
beats.ch02.s05.b028: A sound rises from the crowd, not a shout, but a long breath going in.
beats.ch02.s05.b029: The gaps are prime. They're shrinking. Something is going to happen, and I don't know what.
beats.ch02.s05.b031: That's the truth, Chief. You'll have to medicate it.
beats.ch02.s05.b033: Lavender to the Core concourse. Full draw.
beats.ch03.s01.b001: The long lab is half dark, its overhead lights dimmed to save power. The incubators glow green. Vera sits cross-legged on the floor between the benches, three screens angled around her.
beats.ch03.s01.b002: Her palms are flat on the deck plating. Through it comes the beat of the cooling loops, steady for thirty years. This morning it limps.
beats.ch03.s01.b005: Thump, thump. Thump... thump. Like a heart that's missing a step.
beats.ch03.s01.b006: She opens her eyes and looks at the nearest screen.
beats.ch03.s01.b007: Tritium breeding ratio. Yesterday one point zero eight one. This morning one point zero seven nine. And steepening.
beats.ch03.s01.b008: Breed more fuel than you burn. That's the only rule the plant has. And we're sliding toward one.
beats.ch03.s01.b009: At one we break even. Below one we start eating the fuel we have left.
beats.ch03.s01.b010: She pulls the cross-section data. A line of orange numbers wobbles across the screen.
beats.ch03.s01.b011: Lithium-6 capture. The chance a passing neutron gets caught. Parts per million yesterday. Tens of parts per million today.
beats.ch03.s01.b012: The people who wrote the control logic knew this number would never move. Lucky them.
beats.ch03.s01.b013: On the screen, the old control logic keeps metering the blanket to a fixed value. The ratio dips. The logic corrects. The ratio dips again.
beats.ch03.s01.b014: Look at it. A dog chasing its tail around the core.
beats.ch03.s01.b015: Her slate chimes. A message from the reactor office: MAINTENANCE WINDOW IN 47 MINUTES.
beats.ch03.s01.b016: Forty-seven minutes. Fine. I've annotated whole genomes in less.
beats.ch03.s01.b017: That's a lie. But it's a motivating lie.
beats.ch03.s01.b018: She loads her layer into the sandbox. A copy of the reactor blooms on the middle screen in thin white lines.
beats.ch03.s01.b019: Test one. Here's the drift we measured. Hold the ratio.
beats.ch03.s01.b020: The layer reads the drift. Its gates flicker as they rewrite themselves. The ratio flattens at one point zero seven nine and holds.
beats.ch03.s01.b022: Test two. A collapse. Five percent in a hundred seconds.
beats.ch03.s01.b023: The cross-section line drops like a stone. On the screen, the gates rewrite themselves again and again, thirty times. The ratio dips, wobbles, and climbs back.
beats.ch03.s01.b026: Okay. Now something the universe hasn't done yet.
beats.ch03.s01.b027: She types a number she has made up. The cross-section on the screen jumps all at once, a cliff instead of a slope.
beats.ch03.s01.b028: A step. Everything changes in one instant. Show me what you've got.
beats.ch03.s01.b029: The gates blur. Two hundred rewrites in three seconds.
beats.ch03.s01.b030: The simulated reactor does not even notice.
beats.ch03.s01.b032: She signs the layer as a delta patch. She checks it against the firmware manifest, the way every patch on the Keres has been checked for three centuries.
beats.ch03.s01.b033: It reads: DELTA PATCH VL-001 / ADAPTIVE BLANKET METERING / VERIFIED / TARGET: 214 BLANKET NODES / PUSH?
beats.ch03.s01.b035: She presses her palms back to the deck. Through the plating, the plant takes the change: a hitch, then a smoother beat.
beats.ch03.s01.b037: On the screen, the breeding ratio stops falling and stays.
beats.ch03.s01.b038: Command Node. Tell Kaelen the blanket will hold.
beats.ch03.s01.b039: Tell him the fire in the walls has a valve now. It opens and closes on its own.
beats.ch03.s01.b040: She lowers the slate. Her smile fades.
beats.ch03.s01.b042: Every fall I could invent. And none I couldn't.
beats.ch03.s02.b001: The chamber is a cave of cyan. Every wall is covered with plots, overlays, crossed-out models. A cup sits on the console, empty, never filled.
beats.ch03.s02.b003: Thirty hours awake. Everything is very clear. Every number hums against its neighbours.
beats.ch03.s02.b004: It's almost nice. A fever with a filing system.
beats.ch03.s02.b005: He pulls the raw scintillation counts beside the stored logs. He compares them line by line.
beats.ch03.s02.b006: If it's a message, someone could be editing my logs. Sharpening it.
beats.ch03.s02.b007: He checks a third time. The logs match.
beats.ch03.s02.b009: That should make me feel better.
beats.ch03.s02.b010: He drags a new plot to the centre wall: gap length against cycle.
beats.ch03.s02.b011: First week, the gaps run the primes. Two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen. Days apart.
beats.ch03.s02.b012: Then it starts again, shorter. Then again, shorter still.
beats.ch03.s02.b013: The points on the wall fall in a smooth, steep curve.
beats.ch03.s02.b014: Like a stone dropped from rest.
beats.ch03.s02.b015: He tries to make it something else. He says each idea out loud and kills it.
beats.ch03.s02.b016: A beat between two clocks. No. The clocks agree.
beats.ch03.s02.b017: Heat aliasing in the counter housings. No. The housings are flat.
beats.ch03.s02.b018: The dark count locking to the drift. No. I checked that on Monday.
beats.ch03.s02.b019: Me. My own code. A bug.
beats.ch03.s02.b020: He reads his code from the top, line by line, his lips moving.
beats.ch03.s02.b022: Only the curve is left on the wall. At the bottom of it, where the gaps reach zero, a number glows.
beats.ch03.s02.b024: He sits down very slowly in the worn chair.
beats.ch03.s02.b027: I waited my whole life to be answered. And the answer comes with a deadline.
beats.ch03.s02.b028: He waits to feel afraid. What comes is quieter and older.
beats.ch03.s02.b029: You did hear me. You just don't talk. You schedule.
beats.ch03.s02.b030: He opens a note to the Command Node and types fast.
beats.ch03.s02.b031: Projection of drift interval collapse. Confidence intervals attached. Request full meeting before the window closes.
beats.ch03.s02.b034: I can't find the place where it stops being one.
beats.ch03.s02.b035: The clock in the corner reads 04:10.
beats.ch03.s03.b001: The schematic of the Keres glows white on the wall. The forward spindle is still amber. On the long table, a row of cold tea cups, and the handwritten numbers of three watches: four, eleven, and more below.
beats.ch03.s03.b003: Note from Dr. Thorne, Chief. Flagged for you. Four eleven.
beats.ch03.s03.b005: He reads it standing. Then he takes a ration slip from his pocket and a pencil, and does sums on the back.
beats.ch03.s03.b006: Reservoir at thirty-four percent. Down from fifty-six on Tuesday. The lavender at full draw did that.
beats.ch03.s03.b007: The analog goes faster than synthesis can replace it. The precursor comes from the gene banks. The gene banks have the same drift Vera's chasing.
beats.ch03.s03.b008: Everything on this ship has the same slope now. I'm starting to know it like a face.
beats.ch03.s03.b010: He looks at the feed. Three thousand people in the blue light at the AI Core, humming, as they have since Tuesday night.
beats.ch03.s03.b011: Fifty-nine hours to Aris's zero, if Aris is right.
beats.ch03.s03.b012: Full dose, I can hold the Core for eleven of them. Quarter dose, about fifty-five.
beats.ch03.s03.b014: Four hours short. After that, whatever comes at the end of the count comes to a ship with empty tanks.
beats.ch03.s03.b016: Start a drawdown schedule. The Core concourse and Rings 3 and 7 at full dose until hour eleven.
beats.ch03.s03.b017: Then I want a written plan for which concourses go cold first. In order. Signed. With my name on it.
beats.ch03.s03.b019: Which corridors get a calming agent and which get nothing. Yes. Write it.
beats.ch03.s03.b020: And if someone asks why their corridor?
beats.ch03.s03.b021: Then they ask me. That's why my name is on it.
beats.ch03.s03.b023: On the physiological feed, three thousand heart rates line up into one slow, shared rhythm.
beats.ch03.s03.b026: The feed calls them calm. They're synchronising. Three thousand hearts finding one beat.
beats.ch03.s03.b027: The way a marching column finds the frequency of a bridge.
beats.ch03.s03.b029: A patrol is a shock to the system. It might scatter them. It might lock them together tighter.
beats.ch03.s03.b030: I won't roll that die on three thousand people.
beats.ch03.s03.b031: He moves markers on the map.
beats.ch03.s03.b032: Core concourse pressure up half a percent. Heavy and sleepy. Let them think about their bodies, not their hearts.
beats.ch03.s03.b033: And start drawing precursor from the agricultural reserve.
beats.ch03.s03.b035: Then log that it broke. And that I ordered it.
beats.ch03.s03.b036: That protocol was written for a universe that held still.
beats.ch03.s03.b037: If the count is real, the worst hour is the last one. I mean to have something in the tank for it.
beats.ch03.s03.b038: He looks at the feed once more. Under the calm, he sees the slope again: ground still tilting toward an edge no one can see.
beats.ch03.s03.b039: Get me Thorne and Lin. Here. Now.
beats.ch03.s04.b001: The cool white lights are up. Three chairs are pulled close around the end of the long table. Aris's curve fills the schematic wall, the reactor and the rings drawn faintly behind it.
beats.ch03.s04.b003: Fifty-nine hours from four ten this morning. The intervals reach zero. I've broken every other explanation.
beats.ch03.s04.b004: Every one you could think of.
beats.ch03.s04.b005: Every one anyone could think of. Name one I missed.
beats.ch03.s04.b006: I can't. That's not the same as there not being one.
beats.ch03.s04.b007: Stop. I didn't call you here to argue about God. I called you because I have to choose something today.
beats.ch03.s04.b009: Your layer is on two hundred and fourteen blanket nodes. How many does the ship have?
beats.ch03.s04.b010: About five thousand. Containment. Life support. Gene banks. Your air mix.
beats.ch03.s04.b011: Every one running logic that thinks the numbers never move.
beats.ch03.s04.b012: Then they all need your layer. What does it cost to put it there?
beats.ch03.s04.b013: Each node has to restart on the new firmware. A few seconds dark per node. Air handlers, lights, vents.
beats.ch03.s04.b014: Do it slowly and it takes a week. Do it before Saturday and whole concourses blink at once.
beats.ch03.s04.b018: On the feed, three thousand Faithful sway in the blue light Kaelen has spent two days building.
beats.ch03.s04.b019: You'd turn their lights off. In front of the Core. With a countdown on every wall.
beats.ch03.s04.b020: For a few seconds at a time. Over and over. For two days.
beats.ch03.s04.b021: That's a fever spike every hour. And I'll be paying for each one out of the tank.
beats.ch03.s04.b022: There's something else. One thing I can't patch at all.
beats.ch03.s04.b024: The pressure valves on the Ring 7 vapour line are mechanical. Springs and steel. No node, no firmware.
beats.ch03.s04.b025: If the physics jumps and the controls lag, that line spikes, and my layer can't touch it. Your people would have to.
beats.ch03.s04.b026: Then I'll have people at Ring 7 on Saturday. Not a patrol. Engineers.
beats.ch03.s04.b027: And I'll give you a fall you couldn't invent.
beats.ch03.s04.b029: My curve. The real shape of the drift. Test your layer against what the data says, not what you imagine.
beats.ch03.s04.b031: I'm told I'm good at my job.
beats.ch03.s04.b033: Then here's the choice. Vera's layer on every node before zero. The concourses blink. I take the cost.
beats.ch03.s04.b034: I'll hold the Core on quarter dose between the blinks and spend the agricultural reserve on the blinks themselves.
beats.ch03.s04.b035: That burns the reserve by Saturday morning, Chief.
beats.ch03.s04.b036: Then we meet zero with nothing in the tank but the light. Log it. My name.
beats.ch03.s04.b037: Eleven coders and me. Five thousand nodes.
beats.ch03.s04.b039: She laughs once, tired. Then she nods.
beats.ch03.s04.b041: Aris. I need it exact. When is zero?
beats.ch03.s04.b042: Aris pulls the curve toward him. He runs the fit once more, his lips moving.
beats.ch03.s04.b044: He looks up at them both.
beats.ch03.s04.b045: Fifteen ten, ship time. Give or take four minutes.
beats.ch04.s01.b001: The lab is lit only by screens. Cups of cold tea stand along the bench like a row of small grey moons. The reactor sandbox glows on the middle screen.
beats.ch04.s01.b002: Down the hall, eleven borrowed coders sit at borrowed benches, pushing her layer node by node, their keys clicking like rain.
beats.ch04.s01.b004: Fine. No more falls I invent. Here's the drift as it really runs.
beats.ch04.s01.b005: She feeds the layer Aris's curve: the measured slope, steepening, bending toward zero.
beats.ch04.s01.b006: The gates rewrite themselves to the drift. Then they do something she did not write. They run ahead of it.
beats.ch04.s01.b008: On the screen the layer mutates against a cliff that is not in the input yet. The display floods green.
beats.ch04.s01.b010: She stares at the frozen sandbox for a long moment.
beats.ch04.s01.b011: If the countdown's noise, you go on bracing for a fall that never comes. And one night you rewrite yourself into a shape that fits nothing.
beats.ch04.s01.b012: And you take the reactor with you.
beats.ch04.s01.b013: A body that panics at a fever that isn't coming. That's how you get an allergy.
beats.ch04.s01.b014: She pulls up the sensor banks and starts a filter.
beats.ch04.s01.b015: New rule. You get told what is. Not one second before.
beats.ch04.s01.b016: No projections fed to you as truth. Whatever happens at zero happens to you the way it happens to the ship. All at once.
beats.ch04.s01.b017: She writes it. It comes out three lines longer than it should.
beats.ch04.s01.b018: No time for pretty. Ugly and right will do.
beats.ch04.s01.b019: She runs the steepening profile again. This time the layer holds the drift as it arrives and does not run ahead. The green points settle.
beats.ch04.s01.b021: A layer that adapts to bad data adapts to nothing.
beats.ch04.s01.b022: Now you only know what's true.
beats.ch04.s02.b001: The cyan walls are cleaner now. The old plots are gone. In their place, a field of five thousand small dots, each one a node of the ship, each one waiting.
beats.ch04.s02.b003: The harness. The one job left that doesn't ask what I believe.
beats.ch04.s02.b004: Node by node. What the layer says its gates are doing, against what they're actually doing.
beats.ch04.s02.b005: And if I can't tell the difference, it fails loudly.
beats.ch04.s02.b006: He runs the harness. The dots blink, one by one, then all together. Green.
beats.ch04.s02.b008: He should stand up. He should send it to Vera. Instead he sits and looks at his own checker for a long time.
beats.ch04.s02.b010: He feeds it the residuals, the gaps between the gaps. Then, after a pause, the dark count from ampoule seven.
beats.ch04.s02.b011: Ampoule seven. Failed its heat calibration all week. I've been leaving you out of every fit.
beats.ch04.s02.b013: The checker thinks. A sequence appears. It is not the primes.
beats.ch04.s02.b015: He opens the maintenance log beside it. A name repeats down the page every fourteen days for eleven years.
beats.ch04.s02.b016: It reads: SERVICED BY: K. OSEI. EVERY 14 DAYS. TIMES VARY. NOTE: COUNTERS SLOW TO SETTLE AFTER HANDLING.
beats.ch04.s02.b017: Osei. Every fourteen days. At slightly different hours.
beats.ch04.s02.b018: And the counters never quite settle after his hands.
beats.ch04.s02.b019: He laughs once. It is not the laugh from Monday.
beats.ch04.s02.b020: The ship has a rhythm. A man with a cleaning cloth. And I heard it as a voice.
beats.ch04.s02.b021: He runs a third fit, a fourth. They come back loose as noise.
beats.ch04.s02.b022: Two tight fits out of a hundred. And I showed the whole ship the one I wanted.
beats.ch04.s02.b024: He sits like that for a long time. The hum of life support goes on around him, a quarter tone flat.
beats.ch04.s02.b025: Then he lifts his head, saves the second fit, and gives it a plain name.
beats.ch04.s02.b026: Finding. Second periodicity. Source: ampoule maintenance cycle. As strong as the first.
beats.ch04.s02.b027: Not in a subfolder. In the standing watch log.
beats.ch04.s02.b028: Where Vera will see it the minute she looks.
beats.ch04.s03.b001: The countdown runs in white digits in the corner of the schematic wall: 18:10:00, and falling. Beneath it, Aris's curve. Cold tea everywhere.
beats.ch04.s03.b003: Eighteen hours. It hits zero tomorrow at fifteen ten.
beats.ch04.s03.b004: It's a fit to a sparse series. You grew it by hunting for a period until you found one.
beats.ch04.s03.b005: It's too clean to be noise. I've fitted a hundred curves. One of them—
beats.ch04.s03.b006: He stops, half a breath too late.
beats.ch04.s03.b007: Two of them fit like this.
beats.ch04.s03.b009: She does not press. She read the watch log an hour ago. She has stood where he is standing, once, and she knows the floor there.
beats.ch04.s03.b011: The ship's in a new phase, Aris. The forces are moving. In a new phase the noise gets louder.
beats.ch04.s03.b012: A curve fitted to loud noise looks like a countdown because you ask it to.
beats.ch04.s03.b013: It's a fever. You've been reading the fever as a letter.
beats.ch04.s03.b016: Countdown or fever. The tank's at twenty-two percent. The blinks cost more than I priced them.
beats.ch04.s03.b017: Quarter dose carries the Core to about four hours short of zero. After that, the light and nothing else.
beats.ch04.s03.b018: I need the ship held together for the next hour. And the hour after that. That's the only question I've got time for.
beats.ch04.s03.b019: Vera turns her chair to the console and feeds the layer the newest stretch of drift.
beats.ch04.s03.b020: Four thousand eight hundred nodes patched and verified. The last two hundred by morning.
beats.ch04.s03.b021: It holds the drift it's given. It'll hold the snap, if a snap comes all at once.
beats.ch04.s03.b022: It won't tell us what's on the other side.
beats.ch04.s04.b001: The ship is calm. On the feeds, the galley lines are short, the corridors smell green from the vents, the concourse lights are lilac. At the AI Core, a few hundred Faithful pray in shifts.
beats.ch04.s04.b002: The countdown in the corner of the wall reads 00:00:10.
beats.ch04.s04.b006: The digits run down. Three. Two. One. Zero.
beats.ch04.s04.b011: The hum drops out of the air. In the silence Aris can hear his own heart.
beats.ch04.s04.b012: The deck kicks under them. The ration slip flies off Kaelen's console. Beyond the bulkhead, a rack of parts crashes down in the crawlway.
beats.ch04.s04.b013: The hum comes back a quarter tone sharp, then flat, then as if it does not know what it is.
beats.ch04.s04.b016: A part in ten thousand. Not enough to break a bond. Enough to shift every bond on the ship at once.
beats.ch04.s04.b017: Every protein. Every membrane. The water in every body on board.
beats.ch04.s04.b018: Reactor plasma's hitting the bottle! Containment's wavering!
beats.ch04.s04.b019: Pressure spike in Ring 7! The vapour line valves are lagging! Hatch four's sealed with people on the wrong side!
beats.ch04.s04.b023: The schematic wall shows five thousand nodes as a field of green. Six hundred go red in the first second. Eight hundred in the second.
beats.ch04.s04.b024: It's getting an input it never imagined.
beats.ch04.s04.b025: The red spreads. Then it stops spreading.
beats.ch04.s04.b028: Each node reads its own drift, rewrites its own gates, passes the rewrite along the mesh. Red turns to green, patch by patch, like a wound closing.
beats.ch04.s04.b029: Reactor metering just relearned lithium-6. It jumped a tenth of a percent and it isn't coming back.
beats.ch04.s04.b030: Blanket re-metered. They're arguing the plasma back into the bottle.
beats.ch04.s04.b032: Scrubbers relearned their kinetics in four seconds. But that vapour line is springs and steel. Your engineers have to close it.
beats.ch04.s04.b033: Kaelen is already moving markers. He does not send a patrol.
beats.ch04.s04.b034: Engineers at Ring 7, close the valves by hand. Vent the hatch-four corridor into the agricultural plenum. Drop the far side two percent so we can crack the hatch without a blowout.
beats.ch04.s04.b035: And that corridor's lights at full white. Don't soften it. I want them to see the way out.
beats.ch04.s04.b036: Hatch four open. Walk them through. Slow.
beats.ch04.s04.b037: The room waits. Eleven seconds. They take longer than the whole rewrite.
beats.ch04.s04.b038: Through, Chief. Forty-one minor injuries. No crush. An old man with a bruised shoulder. A girl who won't let go of the rail.
beats.ch04.s04.b039: Get the rail out of her hands and get her warm.
beats.ch04.s04.b040: He keeps moving markers. On the AI Core feed, the few hundred Faithful stand frozen in the white emergency light, staring up at the steel eye.
beats.ch04.s04.b041: And the Core. All I have left. Lavender and blue, full draw, until the tank's dry.
beats.ch04.s04.b044: On the feed the white light softens into blue. The Faithful sink to their knees, not in panic, but slowly, holding each other.
beats.ch04.s04.b045: Hydrolase rates up a percent. Repair pathways relearning their proofreading. Three hundred nodes still renegotiating.
beats.ch04.s04.b046: It took the jump. It'll take the next one.
beats.ch04.s04.b048: The harness crashed. Nine hundred alerts in a tenth of a second.
beats.ch04.s04.b050: The harness comes back. Five thousand green points, each one saying what it does is what it claims.
beats.ch04.s04.b052: He should look away from the screen. Instead he opens the drift intervals from the minutes around zero and feeds them to the checker.
beats.ch04.s04.b053: A spread comes back. Not a sequence.
beats.ch04.s04.b054: He feeds it the intervals from the new plateau. Another spread.
beats.ch04.s04.b055: A noise floor. Where the signal was.
beats.ch04.s04.b056: The stone was the slope all along.
beats.ch04.s04.b057: And there was never anyone on the other side of the cliff.
beats.ch04.s04.b059: It crashed, it restarted, it held.
beats.ch04.s04.b061: The countdown was the drift, steepening. I dressed it up because I needed it to be a letter.
beats.ch04.s04.b063: If you'd spent those hours in despair, the layer could be lying to itself right now and I'd never know.
beats.ch04.s04.b064: The fever put you at your console. I'll take that.
beats.ch04.s04.b066: New baseline. And the physics will drift again on a schedule nobody knows. I need a standing watch on the constants.
beats.ch04.s04.b068: He looks at his display: a slope, rising and falling around a new mean.
beats.ch04.s04.b069: I'll log it as a slope. Not a countdown.
beats.ch04.s04.b070: Vera lets her hands go still on the deck. Under them, the ship breathes, a quarter tone sharp of where it lived for thirty years.
beats.ch04.s04.b072: She pushes a delta patch to the sensor banks and watches it settle.
beats.ch04.s04.b075: On the schematic wall, the dark decks start to glow again. Not all at once. One at a time.
beats.ch04.s04.b076: Deck one. Deck two. Concourse coming up. Ring 3. Ring 7.
beats.ch04.s04.b077: On the feed, the long curve of the concourse fills with ordinary yellow light, a ring at a time, rolling around the ship like a sunrise.
beats.ch05.s01.b001: The harsh white is gone. The lilac of Kaelen's evening band lies across the floor, soft and even, and makes the consoles look like furniture in a warm room.
beats.ch05.s01.b002: The schematic wall glows green from end to end. Cups of cold tea, a dropped ration slip, a rack of parts still lying where it fell.
beats.ch05.s01.b004: Breeding ratio, one point zero eight. Holding.
beats.ch05.s01.b005: Lithium-6 capture at a value nobody on the Keres ever wrote down. And the layer meters to it like it's always been there.
beats.ch05.s01.b007: She watches the number settle and does not say what she feels.
beats.ch05.s01.b009: He pulls it onto the wall. Ring 3, cortisol at a low plateau, loiter time back to normal. Ring 7, falling, not yet fallen.
beats.ch05.s01.b010: No breaches. Chem-bank at nineteen percent. Not draining.
beats.ch05.s01.b011: On the AI Core feed, the Faithful have broken into ordinary noise: people arguing, gossiping, asking where breakfast is.
beats.ch05.s01.b012: Listen to that. Three thousand people remembering they have stomachs.
beats.ch05.s01.b014: It's the best one I know.
beats.ch05.s01.b016: We have a new baseline. The physics has stopped moving. I don't know on what schedule it moves next.
beats.ch05.s01.b019: On Aris's screen there is a slope: the drift, risen and fallen around a new mean. Six hours of it. Not a single prime.
beats.ch05.s01.b022: I want that in the standing watch log, Kaelen. In plain words.
beats.ch05.s01.b023: So that when the next scholar finds primes in the noise, they find the correction underneath.
beats.ch05.s01.b025: Aris writes it. The date. His name.
beats.ch05.s01.b026: It reads: NO ONE SPOKE. THE PRIMES WERE NOISE WITH A SHAPE I WANTED. A SECOND RHYTHM FIT AS WELL. — A. THORNE
beats.ch05.s01.b029: Like putting down something I've been carrying since I was a boy.
beats.ch05.s01.b030: Good. Now sleep, before you find a pattern in the ceiling tiles.
beats.ch05.s01.b031: There is one. Every fourth tile is—
beats.ch05.s02.b001: The chamber is dark and quiet. One plot glows on the black glass: the slope, rising and falling around its new mean. A cot has been dragged in beside the console.
beats.ch05.s02.b003: Harness. Something changed and it can't tell me what.
beats.ch05.s02.b004: He is at the console in ninety seconds, bare feet on the cold deck. He reads.
beats.ch05.s02.b005: Cross-sections wobbled. A part in a hundred thousand. Gone in under two seconds.
beats.ch05.s02.b006: The layer caught it. Rewrote its gates. Settled.
beats.ch05.s02.b007: And the harness flagged it because the rewrite didn't match its prediction. That's all.
beats.ch05.s02.b009: He sits and looks at the wobble for a while. His hand rests near the old brute-force checker.
beats.ch05.s02.b010: Once upon a time, this was a knock on the door.
beats.ch05.s02.b011: I'd have run the long checker. Found Osei's fourteen days. Called it a hand reaching through the physics.
beats.ch05.s02.b012: He does not run the checker. He logs the wobble as a wobble, attaches the layer's rewrite, and sets the watch for the next shift.
beats.ch05.s02.b013: He is almost back to his cot before he realises.
beats.ch05.s02.b016: A woman stands in the doorway as if she has come a long way and is not sure of the last step.
beats.ch05.s02.b019: I'm Sera. I kept the primes.
beats.ch05.s02.b020: I kept them in my bunk and prayed to them. I told my daughter they were the Programmer's countdown.
beats.ch05.s02.b021: She unfolds the slip. Lines of careful handwriting.
beats.ch05.s02.b022: They've started again. Last night, at the end of the watch. The drift came back, and it spaced itself the way it did before.
beats.ch05.s02.b023: I came before the Faithful hear it. Because I don't know what I'd do if they heard it from someone else.
beats.ch05.s02.b024: Aris takes the slip. On it are the intervals from the wobble he has just logged, and beneath them, worked out by hand, a spacing that looks exactly like the old countdown.
beats.ch05.s02.b026: Any slope you feed it comes back as a countdown. It did for me too.
beats.ch05.s02.b028: I know how this feels, Sera. I built the whole thing.
beats.ch05.s02.b029: Here's the truth, and I want you to hear it plain before anyone gives you a version you like better.
beats.ch05.s02.b030: The primes had a rival that fit just as well. A man named Osei, cleaning the counters every fourteen days.
beats.ch05.s02.b031: There's no one on the other side of the cliff.
beats.ch05.s02.b032: Last night the drift spaced itself the same way because it's the same drift. The shape isn't a letter. It never was.
beats.ch05.s02.b033: Sera looks at the slip in his hand for a long moment.
beats.ch05.s02.b035: You gave them something to hold in a bad hour. You held it too.
beats.ch05.s02.b036: That isn't a crime, and it isn't a lie. As long as you put it down when you know better.
beats.ch05.s02.b037: You put it down before it hurt anyone. That's the watch, Sera. That is exactly the watch.
beats.ch05.s02.b038: He steps back from the console.
beats.ch05.s02.b039: The slope's on the main display. It reads out plainly. Would you like to see how the night shift is done?
beats.ch05.s02.b040: Sera folds the ration slip. She does not answer at once.
beats.ch05.s02.b041: Then she sits down in the second chair.
beats.ch05.s03.b001: The lab lights are back to warm white. Fresh plants green the hydroponic trays. On the wall screen, the DNA repair statistics are calm, long flat lines.
beats.ch05.s03.b003: A plateau. Harder than a fall.
beats.ch05.s03.b004: A fall is a cliff. A cliff is easy. A plateau is a slow lie the gates have to be talked out of every hour.
beats.ch05.s03.b005: She patches. Re-patches. Then she opens the layer's header.
beats.ch05.s03.b006: Header. Version one point nine. Name.
beats.ch05.s03.b007: She pauses. Then she types it.
beats.ch05.s03.b008: It reads: THE LOCAL PATCH. SMALL, SIGNED, PUSHED TO THE NODE THAT NEEDS IT. THE KERES IS THREE CENTURIES OF THESE. NOTHING IN THIS LAYER IS FINAL.
beats.ch05.s03.b009: That's what the ship always called a firmware fix. A local patch.
beats.ch05.s03.b010: Turns out we're made of them.
beats.ch05.s03.b011: She pulls up the gene banks. A fault light blinks amber.
beats.ch05.s03.b013: A repair cascade is running ahead of its input, trying to fit a proofreading rate to a plateau that is not there yet.
beats.ch05.s03.b014: You're betting on the future again.
beats.ch05.s03.b015: On the screen, the filter she wrote before zero catches it, three lines longer than it should be. The gates refuse the bet. They hold at what is.
beats.ch05.s03.b016: The cascade runs down and stops. The green points settle.
beats.ch05.s03.b018: You don't get to know the future.
beats.ch05.s03.b019: You get to know the next second. That's enough.
beats.ch05.s03.b020: She picks up a cup of tea. For once, it is hot. She drinks it.
beats.ch05.s04.b001: The long curved promenade glows warm yellow. Shops are open. Overhead, across the cylinder, the hanging gardens are lit gold. A small crowd has gathered around a bench by the central display, not praying, just listening.
beats.ch05.s04.b003: End of shift. The slope held within four parts in a million. One wobble at oh three seventeen on Thursday, caught and settled.
beats.ch05.s04.b004: Gene banks steady. Reactor steady. Next reading at the end of the night shift.
beats.ch05.s04.b005: She looks up. A few people nod. A child yawns. Someone asks a question about the reactor, and she answers it plainly.
beats.ch05.s04.b006: A population that can't see the numbers invents them.
beats.ch05.s04.b010: Every shift. Read it as arithmetic. Not a sermon and not a prophecy.
beats.ch05.s04.b011: When the drift comes back hot, they'll already know the language for it.
beats.ch05.s04.b013: The crowd breaks up into ordinary evening noise. Somebody laughs. A choir is rehearsing two shop fronts down.
beats.ch05.s04.b014: I moved the old patrol protocols to the archive today.
beats.ch05.s04.b016: With a note saying I ordered it, and why.
beats.ch05.s04.b017: I wrote no protocol for the Faithful. I punished no one.
beats.ch05.s04.b018: Some people say you should have.
beats.ch05.s04.b019: A fever that isn't punished breaks on its own. A fever that's punished learns to hide.
beats.ch05.s04.b020: He watches Sera fold her slate away and walk home with her daughter.
beats.ch05.s04.b022: I'm not pleased. Pleased means the problem's over.
beats.ch05.s04.b023: It's never over. But the ship's holding. And holding is enough.
beats.ch05.s05.b001: The cold round chamber at the ship's spine. The slope glows on the black glass. Dust turns slowly in the projector beams, as it always has.
beats.ch05.s05.b003: Aris logs the drift. Then he sets his slate down and does not pick it up again.
beats.ch05.s05.b004: A quarter tone sharp of the one I grew up with.
beats.ch05.s05.b005: Steady. Not counting down to anything.
beats.ch05.s05.b007: All of us, carried through a universe that changes its mind.
beats.ch05.s05.b008: And something inside it learned to bend.
beats.ch05.s05.b012: He hands her the watch. She sits down in the second chair and opens the log.
beats.ch05.s05.b013: Night shift. Week two of the new baseline. The slope held. No wobble since Thursday.
beats.ch05.s05.b014: Her voice does not rise or fall with the numbers. It just reads them.
beats.ch05.s05.b015: Aris listens, and for the first time in years, he closes his eyes in this room and lets himself rest.
